preamble: Denasalization of the close-mid nasal vowel [õ] to oral [o]. The clear case is Galician-Portuguese: when intervocalic n was lost, it left its nasality on the preceding vowel (Latin bona > Old Galician-Portuguese bõa), and the resulting nasal vowel later lost its nasality in hiatus, giving Portuguese and Galician boa, Portuguese pessoa. Archaic and dialectal Portuguese bõa still keeps the nasal vowel. The change is confined to Ibero-Romance in the available evidence; Polish ą, often cited for denasalization before /w/, is open-mid [ɔ̃] rather than [õ].

examples.note: Archaic and dialectal bõa keeps the nasal vowel.
